RASPDACMINI.BAD_NUMBER: {{field}} must be a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
RASPDACMINI.SERVICE_FAILED: The display service did not start: {{error}}
RASPDACMINI.SECTION_DISPLAY_DOC: The display on the front. It shows the cover of what plays with the track along the bottom and the player's state, the unit's address, the time and the volume along the top. The Down key of the remote turns to a second page with the stream's format, and back.
RASPDACMINI.LCD_ACTIVE_DOC: Off stops the display's program altogether: the screen stays black and the remote is not read.
RASPDACMINI.DISPLAY_DRIVER_DOC: How the display is driven. System framebuffer: the system has the display from the first moments of a start, so the player's own start-up and shutdown screens and the progress of a system update show on it, and the plugin draws once they are done. Direct: the plugin drives the display itself and sends it only what changed; nothing shows before the plugin's program runs, and nothing shows during a system update. A change takes effect when the player has restarted.
RASPDACMINI.BOOT_SPLASH: Mark at start and at shutdown
RASPDACMINI.BOOT_SPLASH_DOC: The Audiophonics mark with a word under it while the player's software starts, and when it shuts down or restarts. Off leaves the screen black at those times. With the system framebuffer the player's own screens come first at a start and last at a shutdown.
RASPDACMINI.SLEEP_AFTER_DOC: How long after the last button on the remote, while nothing plays, the screen goes black. A button, playback starting or a change of volume brings it back. 0 never goes black. The display has no way to switch its light off, so a black screen still glows a little.
RASPDACMINI.METERS_DOC: Two meters on the first page show how loud each channel is, on a scale of sixty decibels marked in decibels under full scale. The bright part of a meter is the level, the dimmer part reaches to the peak, and a mark holds the highest peak for a moment. The meters read a tap in the player's audio path, which every stream passes through unchanged; it is in that path only while this is on, and after the plugin is first installed it joins it once the player has restarted. Switching this on or off has the player set its audio path up again, which stops what is playing. There are no meters while the DAC takes its S/PDIF input: that is not the player's stream.
RASPDACMINI.METERS_STYLE_DOC: Upright beside the cover: both at the right, both at the left, or one at each side, the left channel at the left and the right channel at the right. Or lying over the track's line, the left channel above the right. Upright meters change nearly the whole screen with every frame, which is more than the display can be sent fifty times a second: while they move, the screen is drawn twenty-five times a second, and a track's line that runs moves two pixels at a time. Lying meters leave it at fifty.
RASPDACMINI.METERS_GAIN_DOC: Decibels added to what the meters show, from -12 to 12. Raise it for music that leaves the meters low, lower it for music that keeps them at the top. It moves the meters only: what is played is not touched.
RASPDACMINI.SECTION_REMOTE_DOC: Play: play and pause. The keys beside it: seek back and forward. Left and Right: previous and next track. OK: stop. Volume and Mute: the player's volume. Input: the DAC's input, the player or SPDIF. Up: the DAC's next filter. Down: the second page. Option: repeat on or off; held for half a second, shuffle on or off. Power: shuts the player down. After the first installation the player has to restart once before the remote is read.
RASPDACMINI.REMOTE_ACTIVE_DOC: Off leaves every key of the remote without effect.
RASPDACMINI.CHECK_REMOTE_DOC: Press a key on the remote, then this button: it says whether the receiver is being read and which key arrived last.
RASPDACMINI.REMOTE_NONE: No key has arrived since the display started.
RASPDACMINI.REMOTE_NOT_RUNNING: The display's program is not running, so the remote is not being read. Switch the display on, or look at the journal: journalctl -u raspdacmini-panel
RASPDACMINI.SECTION_DAC_DOC: In Playback Options: switch I2S DAC on and choose Audiophonics I-Sabre ES9028Q2M, then restart the player when asked. The Input and Up keys of the remote and the DAC line of the second page use that DAC's own mixer, and say nothing until it is there.
RASPDACMINI.SECTION_JOURNAL_DOC: What the display's program writes to the system journal. Read it with: journalctl -u raspdacmini-panel -f
RASPDACMINI.LOG_LEVEL_DOC: Leave this on Errors only for everyday use. Changes adds each change of the player's state, each key, and the DAC's input and filter when they change; Everything adds every repeat of a held key and every request made of the player.
RASPDACMINI.RESTART_MSG: The display and the remote receiver are switched on in the boot configuration, which the player reads when it starts. Restart the player to bring them up.
RASPDACMINI.DRIVER_RESTART_MSG: The display driver is set in the boot configuration, which the player reads when it starts. Restart the player to change the way the display is driven; until then it goes on as it is.
RASPDACMINI.PATH_FAILED: The player's audio path could not be set up: {{error}}
RASPDACMINI.PATH_RESTART_MSG: The level meters join the player's audio path when the player starts. Restart the player to bring them in.
RASPDACMINI.BOOT_FAILED: The boot configuration could not be written: {{error}}
